verdict.rationale: React's markup is JSX, a JavaScript syntax extension (react-docs-2) that uses plain `if` and `map()` (react-docs-50), so there is no separate template language outside the type system. The TypeScript docs say adding @types/react gives full React Web support (react-docs-13) and that you can type a component's props (react-docs-34), which implies markup is checked like any other code. Missing for 10: an explicit statement that JSX expressions and prop usage in markup are type-checked at compile time, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
